audio_caption: The audio clip begins with a sudden, upbeat electric guitar riff, transitioning to a female speaker who enthusiastically greets the audience before beginning a "friends college dorm/apartment room tour". A brief electric guitar sound effect is then heard.

The audio clip begins with a female voice stating someone is going to Florida State University and that they arrived yesterday and started unpacking, extending a welcome. A male voice responds with "This is the door," which the female voice repeats. A male voice then says "Thank you." The overall tone of the conversation is friendly and welcoming.

The audio clip begins with two female speakers discussing a boy named Brandon's freshman year, noting that he's never been to sleepaway camp. One speaker mentions that it's his "first time really away". The speakers reminisce on activities Brandon has done such as senior week and vacation, but emphasize that he's not sheltered, but hasn't been to sleepaway camp either. One speaker states "I'm the only one", followed by the other speaker agreeing and mentioning a "sleepaway". Finally, the recording fades out with an apology.

The audio begins with two individuals, a female and a male, discussing something behind a door, with the female stating, "we go in here and this is the bathroom." The female, with a helpful and informative tone, is giving a tour, explaining that she has organized the room herself, and needs to tell the male where everything is. She points out the toilet and describes the allocation of space for the male's and his roommate's belongings, emphasizing not to touch the roommate's items. She also mentions the medicine cabinet and extra toiletries, highlighting that it's all for the male's use. She remarks on the towels, then points out the shower. The male interjects.

A female speaker is giving instructions about a bathroom. She first points out "there's Prince's towel" before moving on to the shower. She instructs the listener to "make sure when you shower, this curtain is outside of the tub" emphasizing that the lip should be inside. The speaker then asks if the listener already knows that, acknowledging the listener's likely knowledge before stating "obviously not" because he showered with it inside. They then state "Oh shoot, yeah that's important, very important." The speaker points out "shampoo and conditioner and body wash and face wash." Reminding the listener "don't forget to wash your face." Intermittently throughout this audio clip is the distinct sound of something being placed or moved in an unspecified area.

The clip features two female speakers discussing bathroom organization. One describes the space under the sink, mentioning extra supplies, a big razor, and "Accutane," along with face stuff. The other speaker adds details like cleaning supplies, glass cleaner, and tissues, noting the presence of a garbage can. Their tone is casual and conversational.

The audio clip begins with a person saying "if you come this way, we'll start thing by thing", then they say "thing by thing". The speaker, sounds like a woman, then proceeds to describe the items around her by saying "we have a trash can, we have the printer". They then describe some drawers, one a "junk" drawer, one with "important documents", a drawer with "a random box and some bracelets", and another that is extra. Another male speaker asks the woman if she set up the printer. The woman moves onto describing the desk. To the right of the desk is "big water bottle, detergent, muscle milk and extra coins." She described the items of another two drawers: books, snacks, and food. She describes more books to the left and the backpacks. Finally, the woman ends describing the desk, and apologizes for accidentally hitting something.

The audio clip begins with a female speaker providing directions or an explanation of a workspace, mentioning a "keyboard," "drawer," "computer," "cords," and a "picture frame." She then highlights the importance of remembering that "headless [items]" are in the back, "marking up utensils" are in the front left, and "dry erase markers" are located somewhere in the workspace. She also mentions a "Ronald Reagan" item. A male speaker then briefly greets "Hi Ronald," and the female speaker affirms, "Yeah."

The audio begins with female-sounding speech, displaying a casual tone as she remarks about having "two hockey pucks for no reason" because they are wanted there. She mentions they are "from Navy and Russia." A male-sounding voice briefly interjects. The female speaker continues, describing that one is from the Navy and one is from Russia. Another male speaker confirms the pucks are from Russia and the Navy. The female speaker then describes a rosary, a lamp, and a hook for keys, adding "whatever else you want to hang up there." She mentions a bed, then, going into some details about contents of a top drawer, she says "undies and socks and gum." She notes "that's kind of gross." She moves onto mentioning the contents of other drawers, like "shirts, workout clothes," "regular shorts and pants", and more shirts. She directs someone to open all of them with their feet. A different female speaker expresses "That's so fine." A laundry hamper is brought up. The first female speaker indicates "water polo ball." The first male speaker responds by saying that there are "Seattle and Ladinian helmets in." The second male speaker mentions a clock, speaker, and Apple Watch charger, as well as cords.

The audio clip begins with a female speaker expressing satisfaction with the arrangement of something, specifically mentioning its convenience. She says, "That is so convenient. Everything is very, I'm very happy with everything." Then, another female voice asks "Guys, life flag?" followed by what sounds like "and then".

The audio clip features two individuals, one male and one female, engaged in a casual conversation. The female speaker, with a warm tone, points out items in the room, mentioning "pillows" and referring to a specific one as a "husband pillow." The male speaker responds with a humorous question about the pillows. The female speaker confirms that she received it for Christmas. The male speaker remarks that he wants a husband in his bed. Laughter follows this comment, adding a lighthearted mood to the scene.

The clip begins with a female speaker introducing a microwave, followed by a brief pause as another voice interrupts to mention something under it. There's a short discussion about the items underneath, including "golly gloves" and a "towel neck pillow." The tone is casual and slightly humorous as the speaker acknowledges those items as "extras." Next, she moves on to describe the microwave and fridge, and opens the fridge to point out some frozen snacks. Her tone becomes mildly exasperated as she scolds someone for not sealing the freezer bag properly and warns about freezer burn. The sound of rustling packaging can be heard. More speech is exchanged with some laughter, seemingly directed at a male figure. The speaker concludes by reminding the group about paper plates, bowls, and chips. Overall, the scene seems to be set in a kitchen or pantry, where the speakers are organizing supplies in a lighthearted manner.

The audio features two speakers, one female and one male. The female speaker, in a conversational tone, describes items inside of a closet, mentioning "Brennan's side of the closet," "poncho," "umbrella," "towel," and "hats." She continues with descriptions of dress pants, shirts, jerseys, extra towels, pajamas, sweatpants, jeans, extra shoes, and bathing suits. The male speaker briefly interjects.

The audio clip begins with a female speaker talking in a conversational tone while discussing items like bathingsuits and hand towels. She emphasizes the purpose of having extra towels. Then another male speaker adds that you can substitute them. Then the female speaker expresses enthusiasm while asking if they missed anything, to which the male speaker mentions "shoes." This leads to a discussion about shoes and Derek's half of the room. The female speaker then responds in an energetic and slightly surprised tone, "She did introduce the light", and asks if someone was paying attention. The conversation then transitions to discussing a waterfall bowl. Amidst the conversation, there is a dog barking. Following that, a female speaker, possibly the same as the first one, talks in a casual tone about the waterfall bowl and its position next to a lamp. Finally, there is background noise of muffled sounds.

The clip starts with a female asking what the favorite part of the room is. Another speaker says "oh yeah". The female speaker agrees, referring to something they saw earlier. A male speaker states that they need to turn off the "turtle" and a ceremony. The male speaker starts a chant, and another male interrupts saying "that's the night light". The first speaker continues the chant. The female speaker apologizes if she sings like that, referring to the night light. One speaker mentioned that someone organized the whole room and brought the rug. The speaker apologized because people sit on the rug. Finally, one speakers asks, "back to".

The audio begins with a female speaker asking a question about favorite parts of a room. A male speaker responds in a friendly tone, saying his favorite part is "that everyone helped design," and that "it's like part of my personality." The female speaker agrees, saying it's awesome and will help him stay organized. She then mentions a "Merlin swag". The male speaker agrees, saying, "Yeah, I wanna get one put up right there," to remind him of home. The clip ends with a brief "yeah".

The audio clip begins with multiple speakers, including a woman, thanking the viewers. Another woman jokes that the viewers might never see Brendan again. They then suggest weekly Brendan vlog updates, prompting a man to negate this idea. Suggestions are made regarding the content of these vlogs. The first woman shifts the focus to the viewers, asking for comments about the room tour. Someone jokingly suggests not having Ryan in the room. A woman expresses disagreement and gratitude to Ryan. Then, a woman thanks the viewers again. Someone shushes. The first woman concludes with a farewell.  Someone makes a comedic sound followed by "just kidding, bye". The clip ends with a woman saying "Thanks for watching, be sure to thumbs up and subscribe. See you later." accompanied by a lively instrumental tune featuring clarinet, flute, trombone, and tuba.
